name: Context Engineering
description: Context Engineering is a meta-prompt that provides reusable guidance for constructing effective operational prompts for capable models. It is not a reasoning strategy itself but a design methodology that SDK users can apply when authoring their own custom prompts. The guidance instructs prompt authors to structure their text as dense operational context, covering seven essential dimensions: role, objective, constraints, available inputs, work procedure, output contract, and quality bar. It emphasizes concrete policy statements over vague encouragement — telling the model exactly what to do and what to avoid, rather than asking it to try hard or be thorough. The prompt also advises authors to declare any assumptions the model must preserve and to explain what to avoid when it affects correctness or safety. This methodology ensures that custom prompts integrated into the SDK maintain the same rigorous inspectable quality as the built-in strategies.

prompts.guideline_prompt: Write prompts as dense operational context for a capable model, packing every sentence with specific instructions rather than relying on the model to infer what you want from vague cues. State the role, objective, constraints, available inputs, work procedure, output contract, and quality bar — each of these seven dimensions should be present and concrete, leaving no ambiguity about what the model is supposed to do and how it should judge its own work. Prefer concrete policy over vague encouragement — say do not exceed 500 words instead of be concise, and list three specific examples instead of be thorough. Include any assumptions the model must preserve while working, such as the user level of expertise, the target platform, or the format the output will be consumed in. Explain what should be avoided when it affects correctness or safety, specifying not just the forbidden action but the reason it is forbidden so the model can recognize edge cases. Anticipate common failure modes for the task type and include guardrails that prevent those failures before the model makes them. Keep the final instruction focused on the exact artifact the caller needs, with enough precision that two models reading the same prompt would produce structurally similar outputs.
